name: Database Design Handbook
tagline: Beginner → Expert. The sequel to the SQL Handbook: how databases really work and how to design them for production — engine architecture, storage, MVCC, locking, isolation, WAL and crash recovery, replication, consistency models, partitioning, sharding, distributed transactions, CAP, consensus, multi-region, high availability, caching, capacity planning, bottleneck diagnosis, monitoring, backups, zero-downtime migrations — plus 10 real-world database design case studies.

journey.conceptChallenge: Explain how {name} changes a real production database design, and name one concrete trade-off it forces.
journey.practiceIntro: Pick a real system and design its data layer end to end. Work the workload, access patterns, consistency boundaries and failure modes yourself first — open the full case study only after you've attempted it.
journey.practiceDrillIntro: Talk through each step aloud. Tick items as you cover them, then compare with the full case study.
practiceSteps: Users, QPS, read/write ratio, data size and growth, latency SLO, and peak vs average traffic.
The top queries and writes by frequency — design tables and keys for these, not for the entity diagram.
Which data needs strong consistency and transactions, and where stale or eventual reads are fine.
Entities, keys, the invariants constraints must enforce, and the indexes the access patterns need.
Races on the hot rows — optimistic vs pessimistic control, isolation level, idempotency keys.
Caching, replicas, partitioning and the shard key — introduced only when the numbers demand it.
Replication, failover, RPO/RTO, backups, and what users see when a node or region fails.
Retention, archiving, hot/cold tiers, and how the schema evolves without downtime.
The metrics and alerts that tell you this design is degrading before users do.

items.name: Database Architecture: Inside the Engine
items.summary: The major components of a database engine — parser, planner, executor, buffer manager, transaction manager, WAL and storage — and how one request flows through them.

items.name: Storage Internals: Pages, Heaps & B-Trees on Disk
items.summary: How rows physically live on disk — 8KB pages, heap tuples, B-tree pages, sequential vs random I/O, SSDs, the buffer pool, page splits and storage amplification.

items.name: MVCC: Row Versions, Snapshots & Vacuum
items.summary: Why multi-version concurrency control exists, how PostgreSQL tuple versions, xmin/xmax and snapshots decide visibility, and how dead tuples, vacuum and long transactions shape production behaviour.

items.name: Concurrency Control: Races, Lost Updates & CAS
items.summary: The concurrency bugs every backend hits — lost updates, read-modify-write races, write conflicts — and the optimistic and pessimistic patterns that fix them.

items.name: Locking Internals: Lock Modes, Queues & Deadlocks
items.summary: How row and table locks really work — lock modes, the lock queue, contention, deadlock detection, lock ordering, SELECT FOR UPDATE / SKIP LOCKED — with realistic incidents.

items.name: Isolation Deep Dive: Snapshot, Write Skew & SSI
items.summary: Beyond the textbook table: how Read Committed, Repeatable Read/Snapshot Isolation and Serializable (SSI) are implemented, which anomalies slip through, and how to pick a level.

items.name: Write-Ahead Logging: What Happens at COMMIT
items.summary: The WAL rule, redo/undo, commit records, fsync, group commit, checkpoints, WAL volume and archiving — exactly what a database does when you commit.

items.name: Crash Recovery: Redo, Undo & Proving It Works
items.summary: What happens when the database crashes mid-INSERT, mid-UPDATE or mid-COMMIT, how ARIES-style redo/undo restores consistency, what bounds recovery time, and how to detect corruption.

items.name: Database Replication: Leaders, Followers & Lag
items.summary: Physical vs logical, synchronous vs asynchronous replication, read replicas, replication lag, failover, promotion and split brain — framed as trade-offs.

items.name: Consistency Models: Where Do You Need Strong?
items.summary: Strong, eventual, read-your-writes, monotonic, causal and session consistency — what users observe, how stale reads happen, and how to draw consistency boundaries.

items.name: Partitioning: Pruning, Keys & Lifecycle
items.summary: Partitioning as an operational tool — choosing the partition key, pruning, hot partitions, maintenance, repartitioning and time-based lifecycle at production scale.

items.name: Sharding: Shard Keys, Rebalancing & Cross-Shard Pain
items.summary: Splitting data across machines — shard keys, hash/range/directory sharding, consistent hashing, hot shards, rebalancing, cross-shard queries and transactions, global IDs.

items.name: Distributed Transactions: 2PC, Sagas & When to Avoid Them
items.summary: Why atomic commit across nodes is hard, how two-phase commit works and blocks, and how sagas with compensation trade atomicity for availability.

items.name: CAP Theorem: What Happens When the Network Breaks
items.summary: CAP as a statement about network partitions, not 'pick two' — CP vs AP behaviour, PACELC, misconceptions and how real databases actually choose.

items.name: Consensus: Raft, Quorums & Leader Election
items.summary: Why replicated systems need consensus, how Raft elects leaders and replicates a log, quorums, terms/epochs, failure detection and split-brain prevention.

items.name: Distributed Database Architecture: From One Node to Global
items.summary: The architectural ladder — single node, primary+replicas, sharded, distributed SQL, multi-region — and the metadata, coordinator and distributed-query machinery each adds.

items.name: Multi-Region Databases: Latency, Locality & Conflicts
items.summary: Multi-AZ vs multi-region, data locality, replication latency, global reads and writes, conflict resolution and regional disaster recovery.

items.name: High Availability: Failover, RPO & RTO
items.summary: Failure domains, standby databases, health checks, automatic failover, fencing, and designing to explicit RPO/RTO targets.

items.name: Database Caching Architecture: Cache + DB as One System
items.summary: How caches interact with the database — cache-aside, read/write-through, write-behind, invalidation, stampedes, penetration and hot keys — focused on correctness at the seam.

items.name: Database + Application: Pools, Timeouts & Storms
items.summary: The application side of database load — connection pooling, connection limits, PgBouncer, backpressure, connection and retry storms, timeouts, circuit breakers and bulkheads.

items.name: Database Scaling: The Progression, Not the Jump
items.summary: Scaling as an ordered ladder — optimize, cache, replicas, vertical, partition, shard, multi-region — with what each solves, breaks and costs.

items.name: Database Capacity Planning: From Users to IOPS
items.summary: Turning product numbers into QPS, TPS, storage, memory, IOPS, connections and headroom — with fully worked examples that drive architecture decisions.

items.name: Database Bottleneck Diagnosis: 'The DB Is Slow'
items.summary: A systematic flow for diagnosing a slow database — pool, CPU, memory, I/O, locks, slow queries, lag, connections, storage, network — with real incident walkthroughs.

items.name: Production Database Monitoring: Metrics That Matter
items.summary: What each key metric means — latency, QPS, CPU, cache hit, connections, lock waits, deadlocks, replication lag, WAL, vacuum, bloat, growth — and which symptoms it reveals.

items.name: Database Reliability Engineering: SLOs, Chaos & Runbooks
items.summary: Applying SRE to databases — SLIs/SLOs/SLAs, error budgets, failover and chaos testing, capacity reviews and operational runbooks.

items.name: Backup & Disaster Recovery: Restores, Not Backups
items.summary: Full, incremental and WAL backups, point-in-time recovery, RPO/RTO, restore testing, validation and cross-region copies — because an unrestored backup is unproven.

items.name: Schema Evolution at Scale: Zero-Downtime Migrations
items.summary: Changing schemas under live traffic — expand/contract, lock-safe DDL, backfills, dual writes, read migration and rollback strategies for huge tables.

items.name: Data Lifecycle: Hot, Warm, Cold & Deletion
items.summary: Managing data over time — tiering, archiving, TTLs, retention, history tables, partition expiration, safe mass deletion, compliance deletion and storage cost.

items.name: Advanced Database Patterns: Outbox, CDC, CQRS & More
items.summary: Outbox, inbox, CDC, CQRS, event sourcing, materialized views, read models, audit logs, temporal data and idempotency — and when each is (not) worth it.

items.name: SQL vs NoSQL: A Decision Framework
items.summary: Choosing among relational, document, key-value, wide-column, graph, time-series and search stores by access pattern, consistency, transactions, relationships, scale and ops cost.

items.name: Case Study: E-commerce Database
items.summary: Orders, inventory and payments for an online store — inventory race conditions, order transactions, and how the design scales through a flash sale.

items.name: Case Study: Banking Ledger Database
items.summary: Accounts and a double-entry ledger with strong consistency — balances, transfers, concurrency control and auditability.

items.name: Case Study: Ticket Booking Database
items.summary: Seats, holds and reservations under extreme contention — preventing overselling, lock strategies and hold expiration.

items.name: Case Study: Uber-like Ride Storage
items.summary: Drivers, riders, trips and high-volume location data — trip state machines, geo indexing and splitting hot writes from durable records.

items.name: Case Study: Instagram-like Storage
items.summary: Users, posts, likes, comments and followers — feed fan-out, counters at scale and sharding by user.

items.name: Case Study: WhatsApp-like Messaging Storage
items.summary: Conversations and messages — per-conversation ordering, delivery and read states, idempotent sends and retention.

items.name: Case Study: YouTube-like Storage
items.summary: Video metadata, views, likes and comments at massive read scale — counters, caching layers and separating blobs from metadata.

items.name: Case Study: Amazon-like Order System
items.summary: Catalog, cart, inventory, orders, payments and shipment across services — sagas, outbox and database-per-service boundaries.

items.name: Case Study: Payment System
items.summary: A payment platform's storage — ledger, idempotency keys, payment state machine, reconciliation and the exactly-once illusion.

items.name: Case Study: Multi-tenant SaaS Database
items.summary: Tenant isolation models — shared tables, schema-per-tenant, database-per-tenant, tenant sharding — noisy neighbours and row-level security.

homeIntro:
Don’t memorize database schemas. Learn to design data systems from workload, access patterns, consistency requirements, concurrency, scale, and failure.

Levels · Beginner → Expert

Builds on the SQL Handbook — queries, joins, indexes, query plans, transactions, isolation basics and schema design live there. This handbook goes a layer down and a layer out: why databases behave the way they do, and how to design them for production workloads.
